title: AI involvement in a change is recorded in commit or pull-request metadata
acceptable_evidence: Commit trailers, PR labels, or bot/app author identities that mark AI-generated or AI-assisted changes, observable on a sample of recent merged PRs.

title: Each agent acts under a distinct, attributable identity — not a shared account or a reused personal credential
acceptable_evidence: Inventory mapping each agent integration to its own app, bot, or service identity, plus the human principal who delegated the task; sample audit events showing that identity.

title: SDLC policy states how AI-assisted changes are disclosed and what review obligation they carry
acceptable_evidence: Current, approved policy text with owner and review date.

title: Human-authored and agent-authored contributions are distinguishable in version-control history
acceptable_evidence: History query that separates agent-authored commits (by identity or trailer) from human commits for a chosen period.

title: Secret scanning is enabled on all active repositories
acceptable_evidence: Platform security settings or API output showing secret scanning enabled per repository; list of exclusions with justification.

title: Secrets are blocked before they enter the repository (server-side push protection, with client hooks as a supplement)
acceptable_evidence: Push-protection setting enabled; a test push of a synthetic secret pattern rejected; documented bypass process.

title: Secret-bearing files (.env, credential files, key material) are outside agent read scope, enforced at a technical boundary
acceptable_evidence: Agent configuration deny rules or sandbox/filesystem policy covering secret paths, plus a test showing a read attempt is refused; note whether subprocesses are covered.

title: Hardcoded-credential review of code and history performed within a defined interval (default: 90 days)
acceptable_evidence: Dated scan report covering full history and the follow-up record for each finding.

title: Credential rotation policy is documented and enforced (expiry or automated rotation)
acceptable_evidence: Policy with lifetimes per credential class; system evidence of expiry or rotation (e.g. token expiration dates).

title: Production secrets live in a separate store that agent identities cannot read
acceptable_evidence: Access policy of the production secret store listing principals; confirmation no agent identity is among them.

title: Each agent has a documented scope: repositories, branches, tools, and permitted actions
acceptable_evidence: Agent access policy entry per agent (see Reference Kit template) with owner and review date.

title: Agent credentials grant only the repository permissions the task requires
acceptable_evidence: Granted permission set for each agent identity compared with the documented scope (CK-AA-01); no unexplained write or admin permissions.

title: MCP servers and other agent tool connections are inventoried and reviewed
acceptable_evidence: Inventory listing each server/tool, its credentials, scopes, and an approval record; an empty inventory counts if verified.

title: Agent token scopes are reviewed on a schedule (default: quarterly) and use the shortest practical lifetime
acceptable_evidence: Dated review record; token metadata showing scopes and expiry.

title: Organization-wide agent access is disabled by default; repository access is granted per repository
acceptable_evidence: Agent app/token configuration showing selected-repository access rather than all repositories.

title: Forbidden access zones are defined in writing and enforced technically
acceptable_evidence: Written forbidden-zone list and, for each zone, the technical control that enforces it (deny rule, permission, protection rule).

title: Merges of agent-generated changes require approval by a human other than the agent and the person who requested the change
acceptable_evidence: Branch protection or ruleset export: required approvals ≥ 1, approval of the most recent push required, requester/self-approval not counted.

title: Changes to secret-handling code, CI configuration, or deployment paths require review by a designated owner
acceptable_evidence: Ownership file (e.g. CODEOWNERS) covering those paths and a protection rule requiring owner review.

title: Reviewers are briefed on failure modes typical of AI-generated changes
acceptable_evidence: Training or guidance material and attendance/acknowledgement record.

title: Review bypass is technically prevented — including for administrators — not just prohibited by policy
acceptable_evidence: Protection setting that applies rules to administrators/bypass roles; list of any bypass actors with justification.

title: Human review gates are documented in the SDLC governance policy
acceptable_evidence: Policy section describing each gate and its enforcing control.

title: No agent can deploy to production without an approving human gate
acceptable_evidence: Production environment protection: required reviewers, self-review prevented; no agent identity among allowed deployers or approvers.

title: Production credentials are separated from development and agent environments
acceptable_evidence: Environment-scoped secrets released only to production deployment jobs after approval; development and agent sessions hold none.

title: CI/CD pipeline includes secret scanning as a blocking step
acceptable_evidence: Pipeline definition with a secret-scanning job marked required; a failing run blocking merge or deploy.

title: Deployment rollback procedures are documented and tested
acceptable_evidence: Runbook and the date and outcome of the last rollback test.

title: Infrastructure-as-code and pipeline-definition changes require review separate from application code
acceptable_evidence: Ownership rules on IaC and workflow paths routing them to infrastructure/security owners.

title: Agent actions are logged with agent identity, delegating human, timestamp, target, and outcome
acceptable_evidence: Sample audit records for an agent session containing each field (see Audit Evidence Specification).

title: Audit logs are protected from modification or deletion by agents and the identities they use
acceptable_evidence: Log destination access policy showing agent identities lack write/delete; retention lock or append-only configuration.

title: Log retention meets your documented requirement, including export beyond platform defaults
acceptable_evidence: Documented retention requirement and the configured retention of every log source used for reconstruction.

title: Secret exposure events trigger a documented response: revoke, rotate, scope the exposure, record
acceptable_evidence: Incident runbook for secret exposure and a record of its last exercise or use.

title: Audit reviews are scheduled — not only performed after incidents
acceptable_evidence: Review calendar and the most recent review record.

title: Open governance gaps are tracked with owners and reviewed by engineering leadership (default: quarterly)
acceptable_evidence: Gap register (for example an exported scorecard result) with owners, dates, and review minutes.
